systems.name: Contribution system
systems.note: The 2026-07-30 pass verified R1, R3 and R4 closed — enable stages and proves before writing, sync admits incrementally so one bad mod cannot withhold the portal, extraction finds the shipped form's label by what it says — and found H1: bd77f26's canonicalisation serialises a module, and serializeRegistryModule filters by inModule, so every edit to base content and every # remove is silently dropped. A contribution that adds a path between two base locations is stored as a bare # info, loads clean, and is reported enabled. The fix is written in a sibling file: squash-local-changes.ts:125 does the same serialize-then-reload and refuses on registryDiff, and c9c88e1 promoted registryDiff into the content layer one commit before bd77f26 declined to use it. Its mediums are all 'the rule is enforced at one granularity and not the next one down': the publisher refuses a DSL heading in the notes but not an unbalanced fence (M2), two dsl fences under one heading resolve by position although the comment says two delimiters are refused (M3), and the manifest records what each contribution claimed as its base but not what the portal itself was proved against, so enable/sources can answer against a different universe than sync (M1). L1 is why H1 is green: every materialize test builds an additive contribution and asserts substrings. Earlier baseline is contribution-system-2026-07-29-reconciled.md. The editor and the validation/merge engine are still unbuilt.

concepts.name: the published view is never a maybe
concepts.note: produced by the-shell-is-never-handed-a-missing-view and re-cut after each of its two audits: what the driver publishes admits no absence, and nothing that drives it asks whether a view is there. The type half is a derivation and is closed. It folds '| null', '| undefined' and '?:' into one question over DriverSnapshot's, Driver's and TestState's own keys, looks through a method to what it yields, carries a positive control so a derivation that quietly stopped naming anything reddens the tsc already in CI, and names the fields that may honestly be absent in a pair of checks that cannot go stale in either direction. The scan half asks the type checker what a subject can hold and the grammar what counts as asking, over src/ui and scripts, so a renamed binding, a formatter-wrapped ternary and 'view?: PlayView' all fail where eight regexes over text let them through -- but it is a NAMED GRAMMAR AND NOT A CLOSED SET, and pass 2 measured twelve ordinary spellings outside it. Three shapes escape: a position where presence decides something that the grammar does not name (switch/case, '??=', a destructuring default, a default parameter, Object.is); the nothing put back where the walk does not descend (inside a type argument, a type-parameter constraint or a cast); and a runtime assertion such as expect(<it>).not.toBeNull(), whose subject is an argument to a library call. The edge is stated in full in src/ui/published.test.ts, where the scan half is introduced. Asking the checker about every condition position is the closed answer to the first shape and not to the third, and is deferred to its own spec. What keeps this a boundary rather than a hole is the type half: a nullable cannot be published at all, so what escapes is a reader writing a check that cannot be false, never a type that lies.

systems.name: Testing procedure
systems.note: The 2026-07-30 pass verified the 2026-07-28 closures and found H1: /test runs a # test against the LIVE session state, so it rewinds the player and makes /create-valid-test emit a test that fails on its own first replay — reproduced end to end. Its mediums are one theme, gates claiming more than they check: an unresolvable lastAudit aborts the whole ledger before any verdict, the doc gate or the partition check, and 7676c09's hook reads that crash as silence (M1); layer-check never reads any file directly under src/, in either direction (M2); /create-test is the one authoring command that bypasses the /dsl machinery that would validate and persist it (M3). Owns .claude/hooks (2026-07-28 M5). Its scripts coverage names every file it implements, one by one: the scripts/lib directory grant that used to double-charge the contribution system's modportalCache.ts is gone, which is L4 closed. Eleven of this window's sixteen commits reached it only through scripts/play-cli.ts, which is a downstream consumer of every layer beneath it; the coverage is still earned, since nobody else audits that file and H1 and M3 are both in it. runTest and # test parsing live under src/ and are covered by the DSL load path and Runtime as well. Since then this system gained scripts/probe.ts and scripts/mutate.ts, audited three times at branch level (not a system sweep, so lastAudit is unmoved): testing-procedure-2026-08-03-probe-tooling.md, -pass2.md and -pass3.md. Each pass found HIGHs in the code the previous pass's fixes had just written, and the recurring shape was a decision placed where no test could reach it — inside main(), or behind a test that asserted on a callback's output rather than its argument. Nine pass-3 mediums and lows are open and unreviewed; the branch merged with only its HIGHs closed, by decision.

systems.name: Build & deployment
systems.note: The 2026-07-30 pass verified BD-H1 (base is './' and the built HTML proves it), BD-M2/M3 (every action pinned by commit, least-privilege permissions), BD-L1 (versionCode/versionName derived from package.json) and BD-L3/L4 closed, and found H1: capacitor.config.ts reads NODE_ENV, npm run build sets it inside the Vite process only, and cap sync is the next process in the chain — so the signed release APK is built in dev configuration, pointing its WebView at http://10.0.2.2:5173 with cleartext on. Reproduced under the exact environment publish.yml provides. BD-H2 stays open and wants the same release-readiness gate. Mediums: the two publish jobs have no needs: between them so a tag can half-publish, and neither runs the test suite, because test.yml fires on branches and pull_request and a tag push matches neither; and pinning stops at the actions, not at what Gradle resolves in the job holding SIGNING_KEY. L1 records that .gitattributes and test.yml justify each other with a claim the same commit made false — with eol=lf in the index both runners check out identical bytes, and the real CRLF guard is integration.test.ts. M1 of 2026-07-28 stays fixed: package.json and tsconfig.json are not members, which is why this window is two commits rather than twelve.
